title: Configure Grafana Tailscale Service
description: Configure the tailnet control plane for private Grafana access before the file-platform Service. Enable HTTPS certificate provisioning, define svc:grafana on tcp:443, scope Service-host auto-approval to Athena’s tag:hollis identity, and grant intended tailnet members access. The later Serve endpoint will terminate Tailscale HTTPS on 443 and forward to Athena’s loopback Grafana listener on 127.0.0.1:3000.
acceptance_criteria: OpenTofu apply succeeds with a valid credential; https_enabled=true is verified; svc:grafana exists on tcp:443; Service-host approval is scoped to tag:hollis; autogroup:member can reach only the Grafana Service port; no public ingress or Tailscale Serve advertisement is changed in this wave.
notes: Grafana-only rollout completed. ../tf-tailnet applied the Grafana HTTPS Service policy: svc:grafana on tcp/443, tag:hollis-scoped auto-approval, and member access. The homeserver workflow applied Caddy and Grafana, advertised grafana.tail351aa.ts.net, and verified Athena-local Host-routed /api/health with database=ok and Grafana 13.0.7. Nextcloud was intentionally removed from the active Terraform and rollout configuration.
close_reason: Grafana-only rollout completed: Terraform control plane was applied by the operator; HTTPS Service status shows svc:grafana on tcp/443; Caddy and Grafana converge through the loopback-only 18080 listener; tailscale-serve status advertises grafana.tail351aa.ts.net; and Athena-local Host-routed /api/health returned Grafana 13.0.7 with database=ok. Nextcloud remains intentionally unimplemented.

title: Migrate Athena to tag-based identity
description: Move Athena from Hollis user ownership to the exact tag set tag:hollis, tag:shared-ssh, and tag:shared-conn. Preserve inbound Tailscale SSH and intended network reachability before any Service configuration work. Do not enable HTTPS or create/advertise Tailscale Services in this wave.
acceptance_criteria: The tf-tailnet plan manages sg-athena by stable node_id with exactly tag:hollis, tag:shared-ssh, and tag:shared-conn; policy validation passes; Hollis can still use Tailscale SSH as the existing hollis.wu OS user through tag:hollis and tag:shared-ssh; inbound shared-conn and required outbound subnet/shared-conn access remain granted; the shared-ssh tag is retained, while Kyle SSH remains explicitly deferred because Athena has no kyle OS account; no Service resource, HTTPS setting, or advertisement is part of this wave.
notes: Ownership wave prepared 2026-09-04. Current Athena checks: OS account hollis.wu is present; holliswu and kyle are absent. The existing policy therefore preserves Hollis Tailscale SSH via tag:hollis (autogroup:nonroot includes hollis.wu) and via tag:shared-ssh (explicit hollis.wu), but the existing Kyle shared-ssh rule will not provide usable SSH until an OS kyle account exists. This wave intentionally does not add an OS account. Network grants remain: all sources to tag:shared-conn on all ports; all sources to RFC1918 subnet routes; and all sources to exit-node internet. A tagged Athena can therefore reach shared-conn devices, configured private subnets, and exit-node internet, but not arbitrary user-owned tailnet devices absent an explicit grant. Exact Terraform tags are tag:hollis, tag:shared-ssh, tag:shared-conn, applied through data.tailscale_device.athena.node_id after tailscale_acl.this. Services, HTTPS, auto-approval, and svc grants were removed from this wave.
close_reason: User confirmed Athena was tagged in the Tailscale console and can still access it over SSH; ownership migration is complete.

title: Rotate Grafana admin credential after diagnostic exposure
description: An intermediate remote reload diagnostic used an unsupported BusyBox wget option and exposed the Grafana admin password in command stderr. Treat homelab/grafana.admin-password as compromised. Rotate the 1Password-backed vault secret, converge Grafana's vault-backed container environment through its managed Quadlet, restart safely, and verify admin authentication and Grafana health without printing the secret.
acceptance_criteria: The homelab Grafana admin password is replaced in the vault; Grafana runs with the new value; old authentication fails and new authentication succeeds; health and alert provisioning remain operational; no secret appears in command arguments or output.
close_reason: Rotated homelab/grafana.admin-password in 1Password, reconciled and restarted the managed Quadlet, reset the persisted Grafana admin credential securely via stdin, and verified old auth 401, new auth 200, health database ok, four alert rules, and compliant provisioning.

title: Use supported Quadlet Exec key
description: Athena journald reports caddy.container is rejected because Command is unsupported in the Container group, and the installed Quadlet generator also rejects ReloadCmd. Podman Quadlet uses Exec for the command after the image; use a raw systemd ExecReload in the Service group for this host's supported version. Update the Caddy unit and design example.
acceptance_criteria: caddy.container uses Exec for the process command and a supported Service-level ExecReload for caddy reload; the design example matches Athena's Quadlet syntax; workflow validation passes and the Quadlet generator produces caddy.service.
notes: After replacing Command with Exec, Athena's generator reported the next unsupported key: ReloadCmd. The target Podman Quadlet version requires Service.ExecReload instead.
close_reason: Implemented and verified through the successful public ingress workflow

title: Handle Caddy service bootstrap before reload
description: The ingress workflow applies the configuration before the Caddy Quadlet exists. The first apply atomically installs a valid config, then systemctl reload fails because caddy.service is not found and rolls the file back. Detect a missing service before activation, skip reload only for this initial bootstrap case, and let the subsequent Caddy container apply start from the active config; continue requiring reload and rollback for an existing service.
acceptance_criteria: Initial public ingress apply succeeds when caddy.service is absent and records the active digest without restarting anything; an existing Caddy service still uses systemctl reload; failed reload on an existing service restores the previous file and reloads it; the ingress workflow reaches caddy-container.
close_reason: Implemented and verified through the successful public ingress workflow

title: Remove invalid JSON adapter flags
description: Remote Caddy validation failed because the generated command passes --adapter json. JSON is Caddy's native configuration format and json is not a registered adapter in the pinned image. Remove the adapter flag from model validation and Quadlet run, reload, and health commands, then verify the remote validation and service startup path.
acceptance_criteria: The pinned Caddy image validates the generated JSON without an unrecognized-adapter error; the Quadlet run, reload, and health commands use the native JSON config path; model and workflow validation pass and remote Caddy apply reaches activation.
close_reason: Implemented and verified through the successful public ingress workflow

title: Stage Caddy build context before privileged install
description: The public ingress workflow copies the Containerfile directly into the root-owned Caddy build directory. SSH scp runs as the operator and fails with permission denied. Stage the non-secret file in /tmp, then install it into the root-owned build directory through the SSH exec model with sudo before triggering the Quadlet build.
acceptance_criteria: The ingress workflow validates; the Containerfile is copied to a writable temporary path, installed into the managed root-owned build directory with sudo, temporary staging is cleaned up, and the Caddy image build step receives the installed file.
close_reason: Implemented and verified through the successful public ingress workflow

title: Fix Podman secret sudo shell execution
description: The Podman secret model passes shell compound commands directly with sudo. On Athena this becomes sudo set -eu, then falls back to rootless Podman and fails because newuidmap is unavailable. Wrap create and replace scripts as one sh -c command so system-mode secret operations execute atomically under sudo.
acceptance_criteria: Creating or replacing a managed Podman secret executes the complete shell script under sudo without rootless fallback; vault-backed values remain supplied through the existing environment path; related model validation and a real secret apply/check succeed.
close_reason: Implemented and verified through the successful public ingress workflow

title: Rotate PostgreSQL superuser credential
description: Replace the bootstrap PostgreSQL superuser credential currently documented as CHANGEME before real application data is loaded. Store the rotated secret in the vault, update the consuming model or runtime references, verify administrative access, and remove plaintext bootstrap values from operational paths.
acceptance_criteria: A strong rotated PostgreSQL superuser credential is stored in the approved vault; Athena PostgreSQL accepts it; all intended administrative automation uses the vault-backed value; no plaintext CHANGEME credential remains in active configuration; access is verified without exposing the secret.

Committed 4774d3b.

title: Track Tailscale Serve HTTPS config downgrade
description: Tailscale 1.102.2 imports Service configuration with tcp:443 and an http:// backend as plaintext HTTP on port 443. Reproduction: tailscale serve set-config --all with the generated endpoint, then tailscale serve status reports HTTP=true and browsers fail with SSL_ERROR_RX_RECORD_TOO_LONG. Upstream reference: https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/18381. Current workaround is the explicit --https=443 CLI form in the managed systemd unit. Keep the workaround until an upstream release preserves HTTPS listener intent in declarative configuration.
notes:
Confirmed the upstream cause in Tailscale issue #18381: declarative set-config infers HTTP from the http:// backend and exposes plaintext HTTP on port 443. The Grafana unit now uses the explicit --https CLI workaround. A follow-up HTTP redirect path is implemented locally: Service tcp:80 plus member grant, Tailscale --http=80 to 127.0.0.1:18081, and Caddy 308 redirect to HTTPS. Terraform plan/apply for tcp:80 is currently blocked by the local Tailscale API token returning 401; do not run the rollout until the policy is applied.
Closed as done: Service tcp:80 and member grant are applied, the unit uses the explicit --https=443 / --http=80 CLI workaround, and the full chain is verified live on Athena (HTTP 308 to https://grafana.tail351aa.ts.net, HTTPS serving Grafana). Declarative set-config regression remains tracked upstream in tailscale/tailscale#18381.
close_reason: HTTPS listener workaround and tcp:80 redirect path are applied and verified live; upstream regression tracked in tailscale/tailscale#18381.

title: Create reusable credential rotation workflow
description: The Grafana credential rotation exposed a repeatability gap: the operator had to manually coordinate vault rotation, managed Quadlet convergence, application-side password reset, restart, authentication checks, health checks, and alert provisioning checks. Implement this as a reusable Swamp workflow rather than another one-off shell procedure. Start from the Grafana case, but define the workflow contract so other vault-backed application credentials can adopt the same safe sequence where their reset mechanism differs.
design: Use a declarative Swamp workflow with explicit inputs for the target vault/key, managed resource convergence, application credential-reset operation, and verification endpoints or commands. Keep secrets in vault expressions and stdin/env channels that do not place plaintext in argv, logs, reports, or model files. Make ordering, restart/readiness, idempotency, failure boundaries, and any operator approval for destructive changes explicit. Reuse existing model methods and remote execution boundaries; do not wrap the workflow in an ad-hoc shell script.
acceptance_criteria: A Swamp workflow exists and validates; a Grafana password rotation run can generate/store the replacement secret, converge the vault-backed managed resource, reset the persisted application credential, restart and wait for readiness, and verify old authentication fails, new authentication succeeds, health is good, and alert/config provisioning remains operational; secret values never appear in command arguments, captured output, reports, or committed definitions; the workflow is rerunnable with clear failure and rollback/recovery boundaries; the workflow contract and Grafana-specific adapter inputs are documented in the workflow definition or adjacent design documentation.

title: Move Grafana backend database from SQLite to shared PostgreSQL
description:
BACKGROUND
Grafana 13.0.7 is deployed declaratively on host athena via swamp models in models/apps/grafana/ (quadlet grafana.container, joined to metrics.network, state volume /var/lib/grafana on NVMe). By default Grafana persists all application state (users, API keys, UI-created dashboards, alerting runtime state, preferences) in an embedded SQLite file at /var/lib/grafana/grafana.db.

The repo deliberately runs one shared PostgreSQL 16 instance per design/master-plan.md ('Single box, single Postgres'; see models/apps/postgres/). Existing apps provision logical databases/roles through the @holi0317/postgres extension - see the pattern in models/apps/nextcloud/{db-secret,role,database}.yaml and models/apps/postgres/{role,database}.yaml.

WHY
SQLite-in-a-container means bespoke backup/restore handling for one component while every other stateful service uses Postgres tooling (pg_dump, WAL). Aligning Grafana with the shared Postgres removes that exception and follows the stated architecture.

CHANGE
1. Provision a grafana role and database on the shared Postgres using @holi0317/postgres role/database models (follow the nextcloud pattern). Generate the password into vault key grafana.db-password (same flow used for grafana.admin-password).
2. Extend the grafana quadlet with GF_DATABASE_TYPE=postgres, GF_DATABASE_HOST=<postgres address reachable from the container>, GF_DATABASE_NAME=grafana, GF_DATABASE_USER/BUTTON_PASSWORD from vault. Networking decision: either join grafana to postgres.network (172.30.0.0/16) alongside metrics.network, or go through the host-published 127.0.0.1:5432 via host-gateway - pick whichever keeps the private-access policy clean.
3. Keep /var/lib/grafana mounted: it still holds installed plugins (victoriametrics-logs-datasource) even after the DB moves.
4. No data migration: datasources, dashboards, and alert rules are file-provisioned (models/apps/grafana/*.yaml) and will re-provision on first boot against the empty database. Accept losing UI-created state (currently just the seeded admin user, which GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_* recreates).

ACCEPTANCE
- victoriametrics.container and grafana.container both healthy; grafana logs show database connection OK.
- psql \l on athena lists the grafana database; role restricted to it.
- Admin login works, provisioned Host overview dashboard renders, VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs datasource health checks pass, alert rules listed.

close_reason: Moved Grafana to shared PostgreSQL without data migration. Added vault-backed grafana role/database models, wired machine-apps convergence, joined Grafana to postgres.network, restarted the container, and verified runtime health, PostgreSQL schema, datasource health, dashboard, and four alert rules.

title: Add systemd_exporter and broaden metrics coverage
description: Scrape coverage today is node_exporter + VM self-scrape only. Add: (1) systemd_exporter container with host D-Bus socket mounted read-only, scrape job on metrics.network - enables timer/unit state monitoring and failed-unit alerts per user request; (2) VictoriaLogs /metrics scrape job for ingestion rates/errors; (3) evaluate container-level metrics (cadvisor or podman exporter); (4) app exporters later: caddy admin /metrics (needs ingress decision), postgres_exporter (lab-6lx). title: PostgreSQL operations
description: Epic for declaratively managing PostgreSQL on Athena: configuration management and reload policy, server configuration, application database credentials, backups and restore verification, superuser credential rotation, and major-version upgrades.

Secrets (superuser and application credentials) live in swamp vault, never in model files or plain text. Restore is the test of the backup story: the Uranus restore task validates the backup pipeline before it is considered done. Workflows own ordering between resources; each workflow, not a PostgreSQL model, owns sequencing against other domains.

Split from Platform infrastructure (lab-qc4) on 2026-08-24. Valkey, Hetzner Storage Box, Restic machine backups, machine cleanup, and the platform gap audit remain in lab-qc4. Monitoring moved to its own top-level epic.
Children: lab-qc4.4, lab-qc4.5, lab-qc4.7, lab-qc4.9, lab-qc4.3, lab-qc4.13 (IDs retained from lab-qc4 numbering). lab-qc4.10 (application database credentials) closed wontdo 2026-09-07 — superseded by per-application provisioning tasks lab-6td.1.1/3.1/5.1.

title: Manage sysctl flags

title: Implement Restic backups
description: Implement encrypted, reliable Restic backups for critical homelab state outside the PostgreSQL-specific backup task. Define the repository destination and access method, include and exclude boundaries for /srv/persistent, application configuration, and other irreplaceable data, coordinate application-consistent database backup artifacts, and manage scheduling, retention, pruning, integrity checks, failure reporting, and restore verification declaratively. Keep repository credentials and encryption material vault-backed and out of model files.
design: Use Restic as the file-level backup layer; keep PostgreSQL logical backup generation and restore semantics in lab-qc4.3, but include verified PostgreSQL dump artifacts in the Restic backup set where appropriate. Prefer the Storage Box or another approved remote repository over the same local disk, and use a systemd timer or Swamp-managed scheduling path rather than an ad-hoc cron script. Define recovery point objectives, retention, repository locking/concurrency behavior, check cadence, and a documented restore drill before declaring the task complete.
acceptance_criteria: A vault-backed encrypted Restic repository is configured at the approved remote destination; the intended critical paths and exclusions are explicit; scheduled backups complete successfully and failures are observable; retention and pruning are enforced without deleting required live data; repository integrity is checked on a defined cadence; at least one representative restore, including a PostgreSQL backup artifact and application state, succeeds into an isolated target; no credentials or encryption keys are exposed in model files.

title: Implement machine cleanup Swamp workflow
description: Replace the cleanup intent from cleanup.yml with a declarative Swamp workflow for Athena. The legacy playbook upgrades all DNF packages and prunes Docker resources on Uranus; the new workflow must use Athena's Debian/apt and Podman semantics, existing model methods where they fit, and narrowly reviewed cleanup scope. Do not wrap the workflow in an ad-hoc shell script or copy Uranus-specific commands literally.
design: Create a workflow named machine-cleanup through the Swamp CLI and preserve its assigned workflow ID. Use model methods for package maintenance and safe Podman cleanup. Keep persistent application data and named volumes protected; make package upgrade and prune steps explicit, ordered, observable, and independently rerunnable. Decide separately how the workflow is invoked or scheduled; scheduling is not a reason to revert to cron as the implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-cleanup Swamp workflow exists and validates; it targets Athena and uses Debian/apt plus Podman rather than DNF/Docker; it performs the approved package maintenance and container cleanup operations with explicit safety boundaries; persistent application data and volumes are not unintentionally removed; each step reports success or failure; a controlled validation or smoke run proves the workflow behavior; cleanup.yml intent is accounted for without importing Uranus-specific assumptions.

title: Provision application database credentials
description: Provision vault-backed credentials for application database roles and secrets, starting with the selected personal file platform and any existing application database resources. Verify the credentials are passed to containers through managed secrets rather than plaintext model files.
acceptance_criteria: Each active application database role has a vault-backed credential and managed runtime secret; credentials are tested against the intended database; no plaintext password is committed; rotation procedure and dependent resource updates are recorded.
close_reason: Won't do: superseded by per-application PostgreSQL provisioning tasks (lab-6td.1.1, lab-6td.3.1, lab-6td.5.1), which each create vault-backed credentials as part of provisioning. The generic vault-backed secret flow is already established practice (caddy token injection, lab-e6s rotation).

title: Restore PostgreSQL backup from Uranus
description: Restore the required PostgreSQL backup from the old Uranus server into the Athena PostgreSQL installation. Work interactively with the operator to locate and authenticate to the backup, identify PostgreSQL version/extensions/roles and databases, choose an isolated restore or cutover procedure, verify application data, and avoid overwriting live state until the restore target and recovery point are confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: Backup artifact and recovery point are identified; source and target PostgreSQL compatibility is checked; restore scope, downtime, and cutover or isolated validation plan are agreed with the operator; roles, databases, extensions, ownership, permissions, and representative application data are verified; the restore is documented and no unapproved destructive overwrite occurs.

title: Create and mount Hetzner Storage Box
description: Provision the Hetzner Storage Box used for large persistent application data and mount it on Athena at /srv/media. Confirm the Storage Box endpoint and access method, choose NFSv4.1 or CIFS based on root-squash and permission requirements, store credentials in vaults, and manage the mount declaratively with systemd.
acceptance_criteria: The Storage Box is provisioned and reachable; the selected protocol and permission model are recorded; credentials are vault-backed; /srv/media is mounted declaratively with correct ordering, restart behavior, and network dependency; ownership and permissions are verified; a write/read/reconnect smoke test succeeds; applications can consume the mount without publishing storage services.

title: [SPIKE] Evaluate OpenCloud as Nextcloud replacement
description: Evaluate whether OpenCloud should replace Nextcloud for this homelab. Compare the actual requirements for personal file sync, sharing, WebDAV, desktop/mobile clients, public links, shared/project spaces, versions, trash, search, office integration, calendars/contacts/Talk or equivalent, OIDC with Zitadel, storage, backups, and ingress. Include migration impact from the existing Nextcloud PostgreSQL role/database/secret resources. Do not deploy or migrate in this spike.
acceptance_criteria: A decision records whether OpenCloud is sufficient, which required capabilities are missing or different, whether migration is acceptable, the target hostname and service naming, storage and backup design, Zitadel integration, and the follow-up deployment choice. Explicitly account for OpenCloud's documented migration limitations around shared files, public links, project spaces, trash, versions, and metadata.
close_reason: Revision 2: decision reversed to KEEP Nextcloud. Existing instance (~300GB, ~5 sharees) invalidates Revision 1's greenfield premise. OpenCloud on Storage Box is impossible (decomposedfs needs POSIX symlinks/atomic metadata; SMB xattr ':' names break grants; no WebDAV/SFTP driver exists — verified in code, #1455/#3190/#2173/#894). Nextcloud datadir-on-CIFS is conditionally viable (AIO ships a Storage Box recipe) with appdata/tempdir forced local NVMe + Valkey locking; cutover gated on a 4-item test. Record: design/opencloud-vs-nextcloud.md

# OpenCloud vs Nextcloud — spike decision (lab-6td.6)

Evaluated 2026-08-26. Scope: personal file platform for the homelab
(lab-6td.1). No deployment or migration performed in this spike.

**Decision: deploy OpenCloud (lab-6td.1), not Nextcloud.**

Nextcloud was never deployed here — only the Postgres `role`, `database`, and
`db-secret` models exist (`models/apps/nextcloud/`). There is no user data, so
OpenCloud's migration limitations are moot and the comparison reduces to a
greenfield product choice.

## Comparison

| Dimension | Nextcloud | OpenCloud |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | PHP app + PostgreSQL + cache (Valkey) + cron/web/fpm containers | Go single binary; **no database**; files + metadata in POSIX filesystem (extended attributes) |
| Footprint | Heavier; DB plus multiple containers | Light: 512 MB RAM minimum (~10 users); 8 GB documented for ~1,000 users |
| Desktop/mobile clients | First-party, mature | First-party Windows/macOS/Linux/iOS/Android; Files On-Demand on Windows + mobile |
| Sharing | Internal shares, public links (password/expiry), Teams/group folders | Internal shares with roles, Spaces (project areas with quotas), public links (password default, expiry, File Drop), instance-to-instance federation |
| Versions / trash | Yes, configurable retention | Present; retention configuration not clearly documented |
| Search | Filename; full-text via optional engines | Filename + content search built in (engine/extraction matrix undocumented) |
| Office | Collabora or OnlyOffice | Collabora documented; OnlyOffice/WOPI not established |
| Calendar / Contacts / Talk / News apps | Rich app ecosystem | None. CalDAV/CardDAV is claimed on the feature page but marked unsupported in professional/premium tiers; no Talk equivalent |
| OIDC | App-based; well-trodden with external IdPs | Embedded IdP is LibreGraph Connect (Zitadel-derived); external IdP supported generically — Keycloak documented, Zitadel feasible but **not officially documented**; desktop client WebFinger discovery incomplete |
| Backup | DB dump + data dir | Stop instance; back up config + metadata + blobs (search index rebuildable if omitted) |

Primary sources: [docs.opencloud.eu](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/features),
[requirements](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/getting-started/requirements)
(no database; POSIX FS with extended attributes; network storage only
CephFS/GPFS/NFS 4.2+ with atomic metadata reads),
[backup](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/maintenance/backup),
[external IdP](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/configuration/authentication-and-user-management/external-idp),
[server README](https://github.com/opencloud-eu/opencloud).

## Why OpenCloud

1. Every stated hard requirement is covered: file sync, sharing, WebDAV,
   desktop/mobile clients, public links, project spaces, versions, trash,
   search, Collabora office integration.
2. Materially smaller ops surface: no database, one container plus init.
   The existing Postgres role/database/secret models for Nextcloud are freed
   for deletion; no Valkey dependency.
3. Zitadel alignment: the embedded IdP is itself Zitadel-derived, and external
   OIDC works via public PKCE clients per platform (predefined client IDs,
   WebFinger config). Risk noted below.

## Accepted gaps / risks

- **No calendar/contacts/Talk equivalents.** If CalDAV/CardDAV becomes a
  requirement, revisit Nextcloud or run a dedicated Radicale/Baïkal.
- **Zitadel integration is conditional**, not officially documented: Zitadel
  must provide public authorization-code+PKCE clients named
  `web`/`OpenCloudDesktop`/`OpenCloudAndroid`/`OpenCloudIOS` (desktop does not
  fully support WebFinger discovery yet) and the claims OpenCloud requires.
  Validate during deployment; fallback is OpenCloud's embedded IdP.
- **Trash/version retention configuration is poorly documented.**
- OnlyOffice unsupported; Collabora only.
- Community Helm chart is archived/0.x — irrelevant here (Podman quadlets on
  athena), but do not use it as a reference shape.

## Storage and backup design

- **Data directory must be on `/srv/persistent` (NVMe block volume)**, not the
  Storage Box. Decomposedfs needs POSIX extended attributes and atomic metadata
  read-after-write; documented network support is CephFS/GPFS/NFS 4.2+ `noac`.
  The Hetzner Storage Box offers **no NFS at all** (FTP/SFTP/rsync/Borg/SMB/
  WebDAV only) and SMB provides no xattrs — see correction to master-plan §8
  below.
- Backup: stop OpenCloud, restic the config dir (`/etc/opencloud`) and data dir
  (`/var/lib/opencloud`: metadata + blobs); search index may be omitted and
  rebuilt with `opencloud search index --all-spaces`. Fits the existing restic
  workflow with pre/post hooks.
- Sizing: start within the "up to 10 users" envelope (single core, 512 MB
  floor) — NVMe capacity is the real constraint, not CPU/RAM.

## Naming and ingress

Following `design/ingress.md` conventions:

- Container/service name: `opencloud`, networks: `ingress.network`
  (+ `opencloud.network` only if sidecars are ever needed).
- Public host: `opencloud.holi0317.net` → upstream `opencloud:<port>`.
- Tailnet service: `svc:opencloud` at `opencloud.<tailnet-name>.ts.net`.

## Migration impact

None material. Delete or repurpose `models/apps/nextcloud/{role,database,
db-secret}.yaml` and the `postgres.nextcloud.*` vault entries during lab-6td.1;
the documented Nextcloud→OpenCloud migration limits (no shared files, public
links, project spaces, trash, versions, or metadata survive an official rclone
migration) never apply because there is nothing to migrate.

## Follow-up

Execute lab-6td.1: deploy OpenCloud on athena as a Podman quadlet behind the
Caddy ingress, validate external-Zitadel OIDC (fallback: embedded IdP), wire
monitoring + restic backup, then remove the Nextcloud Postgres models.

## Correction to master-plan §8

The planned "Storage Box mount ... NFSv4.1" cannot work as written: Hetzner
Storage Boxes do not offer NFS. Options are SMB/CIFS (no xattrs, fine for
media but not for application state) or WebDAV/SFTP. This needs its own
decision; OpenCloud data placement above already avoids the dependency.

# OpenCloud vs Nextcloud — spike decision (lab-6td.6)

Evaluated 2026-08-26, revised 2026-08-27 after the deployment context changed
(see Revision 2). No deployment or migration performed in this spike.

**Decision: stay on Nextcloud. Storage Box as primary file store via
SMB/CIFS mount (test-first), per Revision 2.**

## Revision 1 (2026-08-26) — OpenCloud selected

The original evaluation assumed no Nextcloud existed in the environment and
recommended deploying OpenCloud. That premise was wrong; see Revision 2.

Key facts from Revision 1 remain valid for context:

| Dimension | Nextcloud | OpenCloud |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | PHP app + PostgreSQL + cache + cron/web/fpm containers | Go single binary; **no database**; files + metadata in POSIX filesystem |
| Desktop/mobile clients | First-party, mature | First-party Windows/macOS/Linux/iOS/Android; Files On-Demand (Windows + mobile) |
| Sharing | Internal shares, public links (password/expiry), Teams | Shares with roles, Spaces with quotas, public links, federation |
| Versions / trash / search | Configurable retention; optional full-text engines | Present; retention config poorly documented; built-in content search |
| Office | Collabora or OnlyOffice | Collabora only |
| Calendar/Contacts/Talk/News apps | Rich ecosystem | None (CalDAV/CardDAV claim premium-gated) |
| OIDC | Well-trodden external IdP support | Embedded IdP is LibreGraph Connect (Zitadel-derived); external IdP provider-independent config; Zitadel not officially documented |

Primary sources: [features](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/features),
[requirements](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/getting-started/requirements),
[external IdP](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/configuration/authentication-and-user-management/external-idp),
[server README](https://github.com/opencloud-eu/opencloud),
[migration limits](https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/maintenance/migrate).

## Revision 2 (2026-08-27) — Storage Box requirement changes everything

User-reported ground truth: an existing Nextcloud instance already holds ~300 GB
of user data shared with ~5 people; an anime video collection is being split
off to Jellyfin. Cheap bulk storage on a Hetzner Storage Box is a hard
requirement. The platform must therefore be evaluated **with the data directory
on Storage Box storage**, which reverses the choice.

### Why OpenCloud fails on Storage Box — verified at code level

OpenCloud offers exactly three storage drivers (`posix`, `decomposed`,
`decomposeds3`), all decomposedfs variants:

1. Every variant requires local POSIX semantics: atomic rename writes,
   `flock` lockfiles, one symlink per visible node, upload staging dirs.
   Only blob *bytes* can be offloaded to S3 (`decomposeds3`, via minio-go);
   metadata (`messagepack` sidecars), locks, symlink tree, and staging must
   sit on local disk. Maintainer confirmation: opencloud-eu/opencloud#1455.
2. CIFS/SMB is broken by design: SMB attribute names cannot contain `:` while
   decomposedfs keys xattr grants as `user.oc.grant.u:<uuid>` (issue #2173);
   CIFS-mounted data dirs fail immediately with `user.oc.name: no data
   available` (#3190); Storage Boxes do not support symlinks at all (#1455).
3. There is no WebDAV/SFTP/SMB *client* driver anywhere in reva/OpenCloud
   (verified: `services/storage-users/pkg/revaconfig/user.go` registers only
   the three drivers; cs3org/reva's 15 fs packages have none either). External
   storage FRs #894/#2073 were explicitly deprioritized by core devs.
4. Even documented network FS support (NFS ≥ 4.2 + `noac`) degrades badly in
   practice (#1596: "basically unusable... stuttering uploads"); maintainers
   name only CephFS/GPFS/SaunaFS as large-scale-viable.

Not "untested" — impossible without a fork. A Storage Box can only ever serve
as OpenCloud's *backup* target (rclone/restic), never its runtime store.

Hetzner Object Storage (€6.49 base incl. 1 TB, €6.26/TB-month after) would be
the supported bulk backend for OpenCloud blobs, but blobs-only still forces a
local metadata SSD, and at ~300 GB its effective cost (~€8–9/mo) exceeds the
Storage Box option below with less operational upside.

### Nextcloud on Storage Box over CIFS/SMB — conditionally viable

Nextcloud's datadirectory on a CIFS mount is neither documented-recommended nor
prohibited; it is a community-common pattern with known edges:

- Endorsed by the flagship official deployment product: Nextcloud All-in-One
  FAQ answers "Can I use a CIFS/SMB share as Nextcloud's datadir?" with
  "Sure." and ships a full recipe including an `/mnt/storagebox` example
  (`rw,mfsymlinks,seal,uid=33,...`)
  ([AIO README](https://github.com/nextcloud/all-in-one#can-i-use-a-cifssmb-share-as-nextclouds-datadir)).
- Same README instructs moving appdata/previews to an SSD when the datadir is
  on a network FS — adopted here as a design rule.
- File locking is engineered above the FS layer (Redis/Valkey memcache.locking;
  the DB default merely loads the database), so correctness on CIFS does not
  depend on mount locking
  ([transactional locking docs](https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/latest/admin_manual/configuration_files/files_locking_transactional.html)).
- Known live issues as of Aug 2026: mtime loss on SMB uploads (server#48885),
  preview generation failing for external-mount files (server#60846), dotfile
  overwrite returning HTTP 500 with CIFS+SSE (server#63017), `.part` staging
  skipped on WebDAV overwrite via #62853 mechanism, and desktop-client
  change-detection relying on periodic scans rather than notify (inotify cannot
  fire through CIFS; `files_external:notify` is broken since NC33 and never
  worked reliably outside Windows servers anyway).
- Small-scale users run datadirs on CIFS successfully today (personal servers,
  same-datacenter Hetzner VPS↔Box pairs); genuinely bad reports cluster around
  WebDAV-as-datadir or cross-WAN mounts. Failure mode on Storage Box SMB is
  timeout-shaped under parallel load, mitigated but not eliminated by mount
  options (`cache=loose`, `actimeo=30`) and keeping tempdir/appdata local.

Verdict: viable at this scale (one main user + ~5 sharees) **only behind a
deliberate test gate**, because anime-size video writes through WAN-latency
SMB are the sharpest corruption edge.

## Revised decision and design

1. Platform: **keep Nextcloud**, version-34-ish current stable, existing
   instance migrated onto athena rather than replaced by OpenCloud.
2. Storage layout:
   - CIFS mount of the Storage Box at e.g. `/srv/media/nextcloud-data`
     (SMB3 multichannel where possible; options `rw,mfsymlinks,seal,actimeo=30,
     noserverino,cache=loose,credentials=/etc/...,file_mode=0770,dir_mode=0770`),
     uid/gid matching the container runtime user since chown is impossible
     on CIFS.
   - Datadirectory (the share's file payload): on the CIFS mount.
   - Appdata (`appdata_xxx` incl. preview cache) and tempdirectory: forced
     local NVMe via `occ config:system:set appdata|tempdirectory` plus bind
     mounts, mirroring AIO's move-appdata-off-network-FS recipe.
   - PostgreSQL: stays on `/srv/persistent` NVMe (databases never go on
     network shares; NixOS SSHFS precedent and ownCloud forum NFS story agree).
   - Valkey required (not optional): transactional file locking offload +
     shares session store.
3. Test gate before cutover (fail any → revise):
   - Write a 10 GB file by WebDAV/desktop client; verify checksum + mtime
     survive.
   - Parallel-upload burst test (10 concurrent clients).
   - Preview generation works for files living on the mount.
   - Dotfile overwrite (CIFS+SSE combination) returns non-500.
4. Backup: keep DB dumps on NVMe → restic to a *second* Storage Box sub-account
   or Object Storage bucket; CIFS datadir additionally covered by Hetzner
   Box-level snapshots (10 included on BX11, more on larger tiers).
5. Migration of ~300 GB: rsync the data dir (server-side or mounted), then
   point datadirectory at the mount; preserves mtimes (rsync-style transfers
   are reported to preserve them where SMB uploads lose them) and avoids the
   AIO "sure"-path re-provisioning churn.
6. Sharing for ~5 friends is unchanged — this is exactly what the existing
   instance already does.

OpenCloud remains worth revisiting only if the Storage Box constraint is ever
dropped in favor of (a) plain local NVMe growth, or (b) S3-class object
storage for everything including metadata — it has no such roadmap today.

## Naming and ingress

Unchanged from before, now pointing at the real service instead of a future
deployment: public host `nextcloud.holi0317.net`, tailnet `svc:nextcloud`,
containers `nextcloud-web`, `nextcloud-fpm`, `nextcloud-cron`; network
`nextcloud.network` joined to `ingress.network` per `design/ingress.md`.

## Follow-up

Execute lab-6td.1: stand up the Nextcloud stack (web/fpm/cron + Valkey,
existing Postgres role/db models) with the CIFS datadir per this design,
run the four-item test gate, then migrate the production instance and ~300 GB
dataset onto it.

Revision 3 (2026-08-27): full alternatives survey prompted by "Nextcloud is horrible to maintain as a sysadmin". Evaluated against the hard constraints (Storage Box bulk storage, ~6 users with sync clients, Zitadel OIDC, existing PG16):

FAILS outright:
- Seafile CE: functionally the best turnkey replacement (real clients incl. virtual drive, shares, links, versions) but storage is a git-like chunked store (payload opaque to Jellyfin, CIFS datadir community-documented as problematic), MariaDB-only (no PostgreSQL), differentiating features Pro-gated.
- Pydio Cells: external OIDC is Enterprise-only (~€3,280/yr) + mandatory MariaDB.
- ownCloud Classic: maintenance-mode dead end, same PHP-stack burden as Nextcloud, vendor steering to oCIS.
- Filestash / Dufs / MinIO-frontends / Sandstorm / FileRun: no sync clients and/or paywalled sharing/OIDC and/or wrong storage shape.

CONDITIONAL compositions:
- Syncthing + copyparty: only design that reaches the Storage Box via its NATIVE rsync/Borg protocols instead of CIFS; payload stays plain files (Jellyfin-readable). Weaknesses: no public-link OIDC story on copyparty (header-IdP middleware), bus factor 1, no true trash/versioning on CIFS volumes, no full sync client on copyparty side (Syncthing covers sync).
- Syncthing + FileBrowser Quantum: native OIDC + expiring share links, single Go binary; but v2 beta, trash/quotas under construction.
- Nextcloud AIO: if staying on Nextcloud, most of the maintenance pain is self-inflicted by manual docker-compose; AIO ships web-UI updates/backup/restore + BorgBackup integration. Fixes ops pain, NOT CIFS datadir fragility.
- Hetzner Storage Share (managed Nextcloud): zero sysadmin work, several daily automatic backups, NX21 5TB €14.19/mo vs BX31 10TB €20.80 — at 5TB the managed product is CHEAPER per TB than the DIY Box. Caps: 7 users (fits), no Zitadel OIDC (built-in auth only), WebDAV-only so it cannot serve the local Jellyfin library.

Decision unchanged pending user input: keep Nextcloud (AIO as the maintenance fix) with CIFS datadir test gate, OR jump to Storage Share if maintenance elimination outweighs Zitadel/Jellyfin-library integration. Full record: design/opencloud-vs-nextcloud.md (Revision 3 appended).

title: Deploy Grafana
description: Deploy Grafana with persistent configuration, VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs data sources, authentication boundary, dashboards, and intended ingress policy.
acceptance_criteria: Grafana is managed declaratively with persistent configuration; both data sources are configured and queried successfully; authentication and ingress are verified; initial host and service dashboards are available.
close_reason: Deployed Grafana 13.0.7 as five declarative swamp models under models/apps/grafana/ (NVMe /var/lib/grafana uid 65534, MemoryMax=1G after startup OOM at 512M during plugin install). Provisioned VictoriaMetrics (prometheus type) + VictoriaLogs (victoriametrics-logs-datasource plugin) datasources - both health checks OK; admin auth from vault key grafana.admin-password, anonymous access disabled (401 verified); loopback-only PublishPort 127.0.0.1:3000 per ingress decision (tailnet exposure deferred to Tailscale Services phase). Initial 'Host overview' dashboard provisioned (CPU/mem/filesystem/load + VL logs panel), fetch verified via API.

title: Implement monitoring alerting
description: Implement alert rules, evaluation, notification routing, and failure visibility for the host and managed services. Keep notification credentials in vaults and start with actionable availability and storage alerts.

title: Deploy VictoriaMetrics
description: Deploy VictoriaMetrics for host and service metrics with explicit NVMe storage, retention, resource limits, scrape or remote-write inputs, and private access policy.

title: [SPIKE] Choose Gitea or Forgejo
description: Evaluate whether the Git forge should be Gitea or Forgejo for this homelab. Compare project direction, Swamp and container support, migration path, authentication integration, backup/restore, and required features. Do not deploy either product in this spike.

title: Deploy the selected Git forge
description: Deploy the Git forge selected by the Gitea-versus-Forgejo spike. Define persistent repositories and attachments, database integration, authentication, ingress policy, backups, monitoring, and migration from any existing service.
acceptance_criteria: The selected Git forge is deployed declaratively; repositories and related state persist; authentication works through the selected identity path; intended ingress and private backend boundaries are verified; backup and migration or initial-state policy is complete.

title: Deploy Immich application
description: Deploy Immich with its application services, database and cache dependencies, media storage boundary, persistent state, intended ingress policy, monitoring, and backup decision.
acceptance_criteria: Immich is deployed declaratively; application, database, cache, and media services have correct private boundaries; intended access works; persistent data and restore or rebuild policy are explicit; monitoring is verified.

title: Deploy Nextcloud with Storage Box CIFS datadir
description: Deploy the selected personal file platform — Nextcloud, per lab-6td.6 Revision 2/3 — migrated onto athena from the existing off-host instance (~300 GB data, ~5 sharees). Implement the CIFS-mounted Hetzner Storage Box datadir design with appdata/tempdirectory on local NVMe, Valkey for transactional file locking, the existing PostgreSQL role/database models, Zitadel OIDC via the user_oidc app (fallback: built-in auth), Caddy ingress naming per design/ingress.md, monitoring, and backup policy. Run the four-item storage test gate before cutover: 10 GB WebDAV write with checksum+mtime verify, parallel-upload burst, preview generation on the mount, dotfile overwrite without HTTP 500. Maintenance posture: prefer Nextcloud AIO-style managed components or document an equivalent upgrade/backup runbook, since manual docker-compose maintenance burden is the user's stated pain point.
acceptance_criteria: CIFS Storage Box mount survives the four-item test gate with results recorded; Nextcloud stack deployed declaratively (quadlets) with datadir on Storage Box, appdata/tempdirectory + PostgreSQL + Valkey on NVMe; ingress per design/ingress.md (nextcloud.holi0317.net public, svc:nextcloud tailnet); OIDC integration attempted against Zitadel with outcome recorded; monitoring and backup (restic/Box snapshots) wired and verified; ~300 GB migrated from the existing instance with mtime preservation; obsolete or superseded resources retired or justified.

title: Deploy Jellyfin application
description: Deploy Jellyfin with its persistent configuration, media storage boundary, hardware or transcoding requirements, private backend topology, intended ingress policy, monitoring, and backup decision.
acceptance_criteria: Jellyfin is deployed declaratively; media and configuration storage are correctly separated; intended access works; resource and transcoding behavior is verified; monitoring and backup or rebuild policy are explicit.

title: Deploy Zitadel as the authentication foundation
description: Deploy Zitadel as the homelab authentication service and replacement for Authentik. Define its persistent state, database integration, ingress exposure, bootstrap credentials, and application integration boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Zitadel is deployed declaratively with persistent protected state; its database and ingress requirements are satisfied; bootstrap and recovery credentials are vault-backed; a verified login or OIDC flow works for one relying application; Authentik replacement scope is recorded.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed Zitadel v4.16.0 as API and Login V2 Quadlets with protected persistent bootstrap state, dedicated PostgreSQL role/database, vault-backed master/admin/database credentials, Caddy path-aware h2c ingress, machine workflow integration, and verified authenticated Console plus OIDC discovery/login health.

title: [SPIKE] Define PostgreSQL config management and reload
description: Determine how PostgreSQL server configuration should be managed declaratively. Compare a ConfigMap-like directory mount and staged atomic files with PostgreSQL reload versus restart semantics, persistent storage boundaries, settings that require restart, and safe rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A short decision records the managed configuration layout, ownership and permissions, reloadable versus restart-required settings, apply ordering, validation command, rollback behavior, and the smallest model/workflow contract needed for implementation.

title: Manage PostgreSQL server configuration
description: Implement the PostgreSQL server configuration management contract produced by the configuration spike. Stage configuration like a Caddy ConfigMap mount, validate it, apply reloadable settings without unnecessary restarts, restart only when required, and preserve the prior known-good configuration on failure.
acceptance_criteria: PostgreSQL configuration is declaratively sourced and permissioned; candidate configuration is validated before activation; reload versus restart is selected by setting semantics; changes are applied idempotently with observable result and rollback; data storage and application databases remain safe during configuration changes.

title: Monitoring and alerting
description: Implement the monitoring platform for the host and managed services: VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, Grafana, and alerting. Keep metric and log storage placement, retention, dashboards, and notification policy explicit.
acceptance_criteria: VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, Grafana, and alerting are deployed and reachable through intended private or public paths; host and service telemetry is collected; dashboards and alert delivery are verified; storage and retention behavior are documented in model/workflow configuration.
notes: Promoted from feature to top-level epic on 2026-08-24 when Platform infrastructure (lab-qc4) was split: PostgreSQL operations moved to lab-6lx and monitoring became this standalone epic.
close_reason: Epic complete: VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs (+Vector journald shipper, podman journald driver), Grafana with both datasources and dashboards, and Telegram alerting all deployed declaratively via swamp models and verified live on athena. Private access kept loopback-only pending the Tailscale Services phase.

title: Replace Redis and Redict with Valkey
description: Deploy the shared Valkey service and migrate existing Redis and Redict consumers to it. Preserve application isolation through the chosen logical database or ACL boundary and keep the service private.
acceptance_criteria: Valkey is managed declaratively; all known Redis and Redict consumers use Valkey; persistence and resource limits are configured; the service is reachable only on intended private networks; application cache and session behavior is verified.
close_reason: Deployed the shared Valkey 9.1.2 stack declaratively on athena and verified it. New @holi0317/valkey extension adds @holi0317/valkey/user for per-consumer ACL users (SHA-256 hashed vault passwords, container-local Unix socket management, tests in _lib_test.ts). Platform models under models/apps/valkey/: data-dir (persistent /srv/persistent/valkey + users.acl bootstrap with hashed default user), valkey.network (172.33.0.0/16 private bridge), container (AOF everysec + RDB, maxmemory 512mb allkeys-lru, MemoryMax 768M, no published ports), ready probe, and valkey-default-user. Wired workflows/workflow-machine-shared.yaml into the machine root (storage -> shared -> apps). Verified live: container healthy, no host listener on 6379, unauthenticated TCP ping rejected (NOAUTH), wrong password rejected, authenticated PING + SET/GET/EX roundtrip, cross-bridge TCP from postgres network blocked, DNS scoped to valkey.network, data survives systemctl restart (AOF), users.acl contains hashes only. Consumers: authentik is decommissioned (replaced by Zitadel, not part of the replacement boundary); legacy gitea (redis) and nextcloud (redict) on uranus are superseded by their lab-6td migrations, which will allocate ACL namespaces on this instance - next is lab-6td.1.1 (Nextcloud locking namespace, now blocked by this closed task). Admin password rotation runbook documented in design/master-plan.md and design/model-design-principles.md.

title: Application deployments
description: Epic for deploying the application workloads on the Swamp-managed homelab. Initial scope is Nextcloud, Jellyfin, Immich, and a selected Git forge implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Each selected application is deployed with explicit resources, private backend boundaries, persistent-state handling, public or tailnet exposure decisions, monitoring, and backup requirements recorded before completion.

title: Foundation applications
description: Epic for foundational user-facing services that provide capabilities to other applications. Initial scope is Zitadel for authentication, replacing Authentik.
acceptance_criteria: Zitadel is deployed and integrated as the intended authentication foundation; the Authentik replacement boundary and migration state are explicit; dependent applications have a clear integration path.
close_reason: Zitadel foundation is deployed, documented, integrated into convergence and public ingress, and the authenticated Console plus OIDC discovery path are verified.

title: Platform infrastructure
description: Epic for shared runtime infrastructure that supports the Swamp-managed homelab: Valkey, Hetzner Storage Box, machine backups (Restic), machine cleanup, and a final gap audit. PostgreSQL operations live in lab-6lx; monitoring and alerting is the standalone epic lab-qc4.1. This is a domain epic, not a generic parent for the entire migration board.
acceptance_criteria: Shared platform services (Valkey) are declaratively managed; the Storage Box is provisioned and mounted with policy; machine-level Restic backups and cleanup run as workflows; the gap audit records any remaining platform work as actionable Beads issues.
notes: Rescoped on 2026-08-24: PostgreSQL children moved to the new PostgreSQL operations epic (lab-6lx); monitoring stack promoted to a top-level epic.

title: Implement Cloudflare DNS and DDNS integration
description: Implement the Cloudflare portion of public ingress. Inspect the @webframp/cloudflare registry candidate and installed model types before building anything; manage least-privilege credentials through vault; update only explicit public A and AAAA records when Athena's address changes; verify records and idempotence; and provide the Cloudflare DNS provider module in a pinned custom Caddy image only if DNS-01 certificate validation is required.
design: Use Cloudflare for authoritative DNS and DDNS. Treat Caddy's community Cloudflare DNS provider as an ACME DNS-01 module only. Follow repository rules to inspect @webframp/cloudflare and local model types before custom work.
acceptance_criteria: A pinned xcaddy-built Caddy image includes caddy-dynamicdns and caddy-dns/cloudflare; Quadlet builds or ensures that image before caddy.service; generated Caddy JSON configures only explicit Cloudflare zones/records; the Cloudflare token enters via a vault-backed container environment variable; runtime configuration is validated with the custom image; no standalone DDNS API model remains.
notes: Architecture correction: Caddy will own DDNS through a pinned xcaddy build containing github.com/mholt/caddy-dynamicdns and github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare. Quadlet will manage the build/image lifecycle. Remove the custom Cloudflare API sync model; Swamp remains responsible for typed Caddy JSON, vault-backed environment wiring, and deployment.
close_reason: Reworked DDNS ownership per user decision: removed standalone Cloudflare API model; added pinned xcaddy build with caddy-dynamicdns and caddy-dns/cloudflare, Caddy apps.dynamic_dns rendering, vault-backed Podman secret, image/build Quadlets, local custom-image validation, and ordered public ingress workflow.

title: Implement selected file platform Tailscale route
description: Implement the Tailscale Service-host route for the file platform selected by the OpenCloud-versus-Nextcloud spike. Generate declarative Serve configuration, forward through the intended loopback-only Caddy path, advertise the service, and verify certificates and grants.
acceptance_criteria: The selected file platform reaches the intended tailnet route through Tailscale HTTPS termination; Service-host configuration is deterministic; advertisement, drain, and status work; tailnet certificates and grants are verified; public ingress remains independent.
notes:
Shared tailnet route implementation is underway in child lab-bid.6.1: Caddy Host routing, one loopback listener, aggregate Serve config, and systemd drain/reload/advertise lifecycle are implemented. The parent remains open for live convergence and verification after svc:nextcloud, Nextcloud frontend, and tailnet control-plane apply are available.
HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect universal path completed 2026-09-05 (commit ae29bea): Caddy :18081 308 redirect on tcp/80 verified live; bare-name http://<service> redirects one hop to the FQDN; tailnet hosts constrained to exact <service>.<tailnet>.ts.net. Remaining work is still the svc:nextcloud file-platform route itself.
close_reason: Won't do: superseded by per-application exposure ownership. The Nextcloud tailnet route is now owned by lab-6td.1.4 (public Caddy route + svc:nextcloud in one task). The shared machinery built here shipped via closed children: lab-bid.6.1 (single-port Caddy tailnet listener, svc:grafana live) and the redirect work committed 2026-09-05.

title: Deploy disposable test frontend and public route
description: Deploy a disposable Nginx or equivalent static test frontend on Athena and add one explicit public Caddy route for it. Use a dedicated test hostname, preserve the ingress.network boundary, and verify the full public path without requiring an application migration, database, identity integration, persistent application state, or Tailscale Service.
design: Use a pinned lightweight test-server image with a deterministic static response. The test frontend joins ingress.network and exposes no host port; Caddy remains the only public listener. Add the test hostname and upstream explicitly to the typed inventory and keep any DNS record limited to this test name. Treat this as an ingress smoke fixture that can later be removed when a real application route is selected.
acceptance_criteria: A disposable test frontend is managed declaratively and joins only ingress.network; no private backend or host port is exposed; the dedicated test hostname and upstream are explicit in the Caddy inventory; remote Caddy validation, activation, and systemd reload succeed; public HTTPS returns the expected test response and upstream health is verified; the task has no application migration or Tailscale dependency.
notes:
Rescoped per operator decision: a disposable Nginx/static test server is sufficient for validating public ingress. Removed the dependency on the OpenCloud-versus-Nextcloud selection spike; keep the completed Cloudflare/DDNS prerequisite because the dedicated test hostname may need an explicit DNS record.
Deployment succeeded with 13/13 workflow steps on 2026-08-24. Athena-local verification confirms Caddy redirects HTTP and reaches the Nginx upstream, but external HTTPS verification is awaiting operator confirmation at https://smoke.holi0317.net/. Do not destroy the smoke container or smoke DNS name until that check passes.
Operator opened inbound TCP 80/443 after initial deployment. Let’s Encrypt returned authorization rate limit; Caddy is left running and will retry automatically. Await certificate issuance and external HTTPS verification before teardown.
DDNS nit fixes deployed: ingress bridge is now IPv6-enabled, container IPv6 egress verified against api6.ipify.org, and ttl: auto renders to Caddy's 1s duration sentinel consumed by Cloudflare as TTL=1 automatic. AAAA publication may appear after the 5m DDNS interval.
close_reason: Smoke route verified by operator; DNS A and AAAA records deleted, Caddy route removed, and disposable frontend destroyed.

title: Build typed Caddy inventory renderer
description: Implement the typed public ingress inventory and deterministic Caddy JSON renderer for Phase 1. Support explicit public sites, upstream names and ports, middleware, TLS policy, health checks, load-balancing and retry policy, forwarded headers, and disabled public exposure. Tailnet-specific route fields remain in the separate Tailscale Services epic.
acceptance_criteria: A typed public inventory renders byte-stable Caddy JSON; public exposure is opt-in; supported public site and upstream policies are represented without container-label discovery; invalid inventories or Caddy configurations fail before deployment; renderer behavior has focused contract coverage; no Tailscale Service is required.
close_reason: Implemented typed Swamp-managed ingress inventory rendering with deterministic Caddy JSON, strict public host/policy validation, explicit HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, TLS-off isolation, middleware, health checks, load balancing, retries, forwarded headers, and an explicit Caddy validation method.

title: Deploy Caddy configuration with rollback
description: Implement the Caddy configuration model operations for candidate staging, local and remote validation, atomic activation, graceful reload, active digest recording, and rollback. Follow the candidate caddy.json.next and directory bind-mount sequence in design/ingress.md and use the shared @holi0317/remote-ssh adapter through @swamp/ssh.
acceptance_criteria: The renderer rejects malformed JSON locally; the candidate is validated on Athena using the pinned custom Caddy image and vault-backed Podman secret; activation uses atomic rename; reload uses systemctl reload caddy.service without restarting the container; the active digest is recorded; failed reload restores the prior known-good file; operations do not invoke local ssh, scp, rsync, or local Podman.
notes:
Removed local Podman/Caddy execution from the renderer. Local execution now validates JSON syntax only; the custom xcaddy image validates the candidate on Athena through @swamp/ssh before activation. This keeps runtime ownership on the target host.
Validation run on 2026-08-24: local renderer tests, Deno typecheck, ingress-config model validation, workflow validation, render, and persisted JSON validation all succeeded. Remote Athena checks are blocked because Tailscale SSH requires re-authentication. Secret apply is also blocked because homelab vault lacks cloudflare.api-token; only postgres.nextcloud.password and postgres.superuser exist. Resume remote validation after re-auth and adding the vault-backed Cloudflare token.
Operator identified the Quadlet generator failure via journald. Athena reported unsupported Command, then unsupported ReloadCmd; the unit now uses Exec plus Service.ExecReload. Full machine-ingress-public workflow completed 11/11 steps successfully. caddy.service is loaded and running, and remote http://127.0.0.1/healthz returned ok. Cloudflare secret is vault-backed and applied successfully.
close_reason: Caddy configuration rollout, bootstrap handling, remote validation, atomic activation, systemd reload path, custom image, secret, and running Quadlet are implemented; machine-ingress-public completed 11/11 steps and the health smoke test passed.

title: Define ingress network and Caddy Quadlet
description: Implement the rootful system Quadlet and Podman ingress.network described in design/ingress.md. Caddy must use persistent data and config directories, bind the config directory read-only, publish only ports 80 and 443, join ingress.network, use the pinned Caddy image, and expose reload through systemctl reload without a public admin API or Podman API socket.
acceptance_criteria: The ingress network exists declaratively; the Caddy Quadlet renders a service with persistent restricted state, only host ports 80/443, no Podman socket, no public admin API, and a reload command; Caddy starts with a minimal valid configuration; application backends remain off the public host interface.
close_reason: Implemented declarative ingress.network, persistent Caddy data/config preparation, pinned rootful Caddy Quadlet, private admin reload endpoint, and minimal health configuration; Swamp model validation passed.

title: Public Caddy ingress and Cloudflare DNS
description: Epic for public-internet ingress on Athena. Caddy owns the explicit reverse-proxy edge, public HTTPS, routing, middleware, health checks, generated configuration, reloads, and rollback. Cloudflare owns authoritative DNS and DDNS for explicit public records. Tailscale Services is intentionally outside this epic.
design: Follow the Phase 1 section of design/ingress.md. Caddy owns public routing, ACME, middleware, health checks, generated configuration, reloads, and rollback. Cloudflare DNS/DDNS owns explicit public A/AAAA updates and record verification. Use the Cloudflare Caddy DNS module only for ACME DNS-01 when needed, not as a DDNS mechanism. Use shared @holi0317/remote-ssh execution.
acceptance_criteria: Public Caddy ingress is deployed with explicit routes, persistent restricted state, safe configuration rollout and rollback, Cloudflare DNS/DDNS convergence, public ACME, and verified application access. No tailnet Service is required for completion.
notes:
Public ingress is a standalone epic. Platform infrastructure, foundation applications, application deployments, Tailscale Services, and go links are separate domain epics; this board does not use a generic Swamp-migration parent epic.
Architecture correction on 2026-08-19: Caddy owns DDNS through pinned xcaddy modules caddy-dynamicdns and caddy-dns/cloudflare; Cloudflare remains the authoritative DNS provider. The standalone Swamp Cloudflare API model was removed. Quadlet builds the custom image and injects the vault-backed token secret.
Operator decision: replace the oversized selected-file-platform route with a disposable Nginx/static ingress smoke fixture under lab-bid.5. lab-bid.8 is not applicable because there are no existing public applications to migrate and was closed.
close_reason: All six ingress epic child issues are complete; public smoke route was verified and then fully torn down.

title: Add Valkey cache for Zitadel
description: Enable Zitadel's distributed cache against the shared Valkey instance. Zitadel (deployed v4.16.0) supports Redis/Valkey cache connectors via ZITADEL_CACHES_CONNECTORS_REDIS_ADDR/USERNAME/PASSWORD. First verify the cache actually helps a single-node Zitadel (distributed caching mainly benefits multi-replica setups; the in-memory default may suffice) - if not, close with the recorded decision. If wiring it: allocate a zitadel ACL user and logical DB on the shared Valkey (lab-qc4.2 mechanism), pass credentials as vault-backed managed secrets, add the env vars to the zitadel-api and zitadel-login models, and verify cache activity plus the auth boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Zitadel cache support evaluated against the single-node deployment with the decision recorded; if wired: zitadel ACL user + logical DB allocated, credentials reach containers as managed secrets, cache activity and ACL isolation verified.

title: Grafana deployment follow-ups
description: Container for follow-up work on the deployed Grafana stack. The initial deployment (container, VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs datasources, alerting, SQLite-to-Postgres migration, svc:grafana tailnet exposure) shipped under the closed lab-qc4.1 monitoring epic. This epic owns the remaining Grafana items: SSO via Zitadel OIDC (lab-qc4.15) and dashboard-as-code adoption via Git Sync (lab-b6o). Swamp stays the authority for deployment, datasources, alerting, and storage.

title: Adopt Grafana Git Sync for dashboards and folders
description: Evaluate and implement Grafana Git Sync for dashboard and folder resources while retaining Swamp-managed provisioning for Grafana deployment, datasources, alert rules, contact points, and notification policies. Grafana Git Sync is currently limited to dashboards and folders, which is sufficient for the first adoption and may be an initial foundation for broader observability-as-code resource support in future Grafana releases. Migrate the existing host overview dashboard deliberately, avoid simultaneous classic-provider and Git Sync ownership, and preserve datasource UIDs and dashboard behavior. Prefer a branch/PR workflow and explicit secret handling. Do not migrate unsupported resources or introduce a general Grafana API control plane as part of this issue.
design: Use Grafana Git Sync's native Repository resource and gcx setup path, with GitHub enhanced integration or Pure Git as appropriate for the selected repository. Keep Swamp as the authority for the Grafana container, database, datasources, alerting, plugins, and credentials not required by Git Sync. Store dashboards as standalone JSON under an isolated repository path or dedicated dashboard repository. Because the current dashboard is embedded in models/apps/grafana/dashboard-host.yaml and classic file provisioning is read-only from the container, export/import the dashboard and perform a controlled ownership cutover. Configure polling initially; add webhooks only if the ingress boundary is intentionally changed. Reassess broader resource migration only when Grafana officially supports those resources and the repository control-plane boundary is clear.
acceptance_criteria: Grafana Git Sync is configured and validated for dashboards and folders; the existing host overview dashboard is migrated without duplicate-UID ownership or loss of panels, datasource references, folder placement, or dashboard availability; a Git change is synchronized into Grafana; an approved UI change follows the selected direct-commit or pull-request workflow and is represented in Git; classic Swamp provisioning remains authoritative and operational for datasources, alert rules, contact points, notification policies, Grafana deployment, plugins, and secrets; no unsupported Grafana resources are moved; repository credentials are least-privilege and do not appear in model files, command arguments, or reports; the final repository path, branch, sync interval, ownership boundary, rollback procedure, and known Git Sync limitations are documented; Grafana health and dashboard query behavior remain verified after cutover.

title: Host PJJ periodic downloader
description: Host the pjj Go batch downloader as a container run by a systemd timer. Build or pin the source, inject Pixiv and Fanbox session tokens from vault, persist TOML configuration, seen-ID files, and downloaded output, and provide overlap protection, logs, retries, and failure visibility.
acceptance_criteria: A pinned PJJ image runs successfully from a declarative container and systemd timer; configuration and both seen files persist; tokens are not stored in model files; downloads land in the intended storage; concurrent timer runs are prevented; logs and failures are observable; restart and upgrade behavior are documented.

title: [SPIKE] Audit missing platform infrastructure work
description: Review the master plan and current Beads board for missing shared infrastructure needed to operate the homelab: storage, secrets, networking, backups, upgrades, logging, alerting, and recovery. Do not implement anything in this spike.
acceptance_criteria: The audit produces a concise list of missing or intentionally deferred platform capabilities, with one Beads follow-up per actionable gap and explicit rationale for items that remain out of scope.

title: Implement PostgreSQL backups
description: Implement reliable PostgreSQL backup and restore operations for the shared PostgreSQL server and application databases. Define destination, retention, encryption or credential handling, scheduling, failure reporting, and a restore verification path.
acceptance_criteria: Backups run on the intended schedule; credentials and destinations are vault-backed; failures are observable; retention is enforced; at least one restore verification proves a usable database backup; application databases are covered without exposing secrets in model files.

title: Tailscale Services exposure
description: Epic for deferred private tailnet exposure after public Caddy ingress is stable. Own the Tailscale Service-host prerequisites, declarative Serve configuration, svc:nextcloud advertisement and drain lifecycle, tailnet Caddy routing, certificates, grants, and status. Go links are tracked in a separate epic.
design: Follow the Phase 2 section of design/ingress.md. Keep Tailscale Service-host configuration separate from the control-plane Service definition. Depend on the completed public feature, use loopback-only Caddy handoff, and preserve the shared remote execution boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Athena is approved as a Service host; svc:nextcloud reaches the intended tailnet route through Tailscale HTTPS termination; Service-host apply, advertise, drain, and status behavior is verified; tailnet certificates and grants are correct; public ingress remains independent of this epic.
notes:
Go links moved to separate epic homeserver-compose-m5v; the Tailscale epic ends at Service-host exposure and tailnet routing.
Kept as a top-level epic. Sequencing after public ingress is enforced by its child Service-host route depending on the public file-platform route, rather than by an epic-to-epic dependency.
close_reason: Won't do: the standalone Tailscale Services phase is superseded by per-application tailnet exposure (svc:<app> owned inside each app's deployment task, e.g. lab-6td.1.4, lab-6td.3.4, lab-6td.5.3). Completed machinery (single-port tailnet listener, reload method, svc:grafana) lives on via closed children.

title: Migrate remaining public applications to ingress
description: Migrate additional public-facing applications one at a time using the explicit Caddy inventory and shared ingress.network. Define public exposure deliberately, preserve private backend networks, validate the generated configuration, deploy with rollback protection, and verify public HTTPS and upstream health before moving to the next application. Tailnet-only exposure belongs to the deferred Tailscale Services feature.
acceptance_criteria: Every migrated public application has an explicit Caddy route and verified upstream health; no backend or arbitrary container is publicly published; Cloudflare DNS and public ACME state are valid; each migration can be rolled back independently; tailnet-only routes are not introduced in this public migration task.
close_reason: No remaining public applications exist to migrate; public ingress will be validated with the disposable test frontend tracked by lab-bid.5.

title: Implement go/nextcloud redirect
description: Implement the first go-link target: redirect go/nextcloud to the configured long-form Nextcloud ts.net FQDN through the tailnet-only path. Keep the implementation extensible for additional approved shortcuts without introducing a general URL-shortener database or public service.
acceptance_criteria: go/nextcloud matches only the intended exact path, redirects to the configured Nextcloud ts.net FQDN with stable 308 behavior, rejects unknown paths, is reachable only through the intended tailnet service path, and is generated deterministically from the approved link map.
close_reason: Won't do: go/nextcloud is not needed now. Caddy's bare-name tailnet redirects (http://grafana, completed 2026-09-05) already cover the immediate convenience; go-link namespace remains a P4 backlog nice-to-have under lab-m5v.

title: Move Hetzner Cloud resources into Swamp
description: Epic for declaratively managing Hetzner Cloud resources (Cloud server, Volume, private Network, Firewall, snapshots/backups) through swamp models and workflows. These resources are provisioned manually in the Hetzner Cloud console today and are explicitly out of scope for all current epics; this epic tracks moving them under Swamp control.
design: Search for an existing community extension first (swamp extension search hetzner); prefer @swamp/* official models before writing custom extensions in extensions/models/. Any custom model follows the Ansible/Terraform idioms from design/model-design-principles.md (idempotent apply, explicit ensure, state resources) and reuses the shared @holi0317/remote-ssh execution boundary where remote access is needed. Credentials (API token) live in swamp vault. Migration must not recreate the running Athena server destructively: adopt existing resources first, then converge.
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope Hetzner Cloud resources are represented as swamp models with idempotent apply/drift detection; adopting existing Athena infrastructure does not recreate or destroy it; API token is vault-backed; a documented workflow can reconcile desired vs actual state.
notes: Explicitly deferred: no current epic owns Hetzner Cloud API resources. Sequencing against Platform infrastructure (lab-qc4) is by child dependencies if ever needed, not an epic-to-epic dependency; this board does not use a generic migration parent.

title: Create Swamp workflow for PostgreSQL major-version upgrades
description: Define and implement a Swamp workflow for upgrading the shared PostgreSQL service across major versions. Cover preflight checks, backup and restore readiness, compatibility and extension checks, controlled migration or cutover, rollback boundaries, service downtime, and post-upgrade verification. Keep the workflow rerunnable and explicit about operator approvals for destructive or irreversible steps.
acceptance_criteria: A validated Swamp workflow exists for PostgreSQL major-version upgrades; it performs or verifies backups before migration; checks source and target versions plus extensions; makes downtime, cutover, rollback, and operator approval boundaries explicit; and verifies roles, databases, extensions, ownership, permissions, and representative application queries after upgrade.
